google.label: Searching on Google
google.body: Ten blue links, ranked. Twenty years of SEO practice tells you how to compete here.

ai.label: Asking AI
ai.body: One synthesized answer. No ranking, no page two. Either the AI names you, or you don't exist.

observe.body: We learn your business the way an engineer would — processes, systems, data, and where the money actually moves.

analyze.label: Analyze

aiConsultancy.problem: Every consultancy will tell you AI changes everything. Almost none will tell you, in numbers, what it's worth in YOUR operation — before you commit to building anything. We do the analysis first: your processes, your data, your costs. Then we show you where AI pays, what it costs to capture, and how we'd measure success. If the numbers don't work, we tell you that too.

demo.heading: What an audit actually finds.

rows.label: the situation
rows.body: A contract beverage manufacturer runs 70–80% of its volume through one robotic line. Schedulers hand-price every short run, and quoting takes days.

rows.label: the model
rows.body: Our model was built from their public statements and industry benchmarks, then corrected live with their real numbers.

rows.label: the finding
rows.body: Even at the most conservative baseline, it showed an RFQ-and-scheduling engine returning its cost in under nine months.

demo.closing: Every audit works the same way: your operation, your numbers, a sensitivity table that includes the case where we tell you not to build.

steps.label: Observe
steps.body: Two weeks inside your processes, systems, and data flows.

steps.label: Analyze
steps.body: The opportunity map: what AI can genuinely do here, ranked.

steps.label: Quantify
steps.body: The ROI model, benchmark defaults replaced by your actuals.

steps.label: Build
steps.body: A fixed-price proposal. Take it, phase it, or walk with the analysis.

price.note: Every dollar credits toward your first build or retainer within 90 days. If we work together, the audit was free.

deliverables: Everything is yours to keep either way.

measurement.heading: The model shows its work.
measurement.body: Every number in your audit is labeled: audited public fact, industry benchmark, or engineering model — with the source. We present the formula, not just the total, and we plug in your actual figures live.

faq.question: What if the numbers say AI isn't worth it for us?
faq.answer: Then the audit says that, in writing. You'll have spent $2,500 to avoid spending $50,000. We think that's a good trade, and you keep the analysis.

faq.question: Do you only work with manufacturers?
faq.answer: No — any business with repeatable processes and real data. The method is the same; the opportunities differ.

faq.question: We're not in Indiana. Does that matter?
faq.answer: No. We're based in Indianapolis and work with businesses worldwide. Everything here is priced and delivered the same way globally.

aiConsultancy.headline: Most AI advice starts with the technology. Ours starts with your P&L.

aiSearchVisibility.problem: Nearly half of consumers now ask AI assistants for recommendations, and most businesses never appear in the answers. The work that fixes it is measurable: we test the exact prompts your customers use, show you where you stand, do the technical and content work both Google and AI engines reward, and re-test on a schedule you can verify yourself.

demo.heading: Try it right now.
steps: Ask for the best option in your category and city.
If you're not in the answer, that's the problem.
demo.closing: Nearly half of consumers now ask AI tools for local recommendations. Being excellent on Google no longer means you exist where a growing share of your customers actually ask.

steps.label: Baseline
steps.body: We run a fixed set of twenty prompts your buyers would use, three times each across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity, and record exactly where you stand. You get the prompt set on day one.

steps.label: Foundation
steps.body: The technical and entity work both rails reward: structured data, crawlability (graded by our own tool), citations, reviews, consistency everywhere your business is named.

steps.label: Content
steps.body: Pages and answers built for how engines actually retrieve, validated against real search volume before anything is written.

steps.label: Re-measure
steps.body: Same prompts, every month, in your report. Run them yourself any time.

price.note: Google and AI search, worked as one program. Measured monthly against a fixed prompt set you can run yourself.

measurement.heading: You hold the yardstick.
measurement.body: The prompt set is fixed on day one and never changes without your sign-off. Outputs vary run to run, so we measure three runs per prompt and report the rate across all three. There is no proprietary “visibility score”. The report states whether you were named, where, and what you were cited from. We can't fake this and wouldn't try.

faq.question: Can you guarantee I'll show up in ChatGPT?
faq.answer: No, and nobody honestly can. The systems are non-deterministic. What we guarantee is the measurement: you'll know exactly where you stand, before and after, verifiably.

faq.question: Is this different from SEO?
faq.answer: It's SEO plus the AI rail, worked as one program. Most of the foundational work overlaps, which is why we don't sell them separately.

faq.question: How fast do results show?
faq.answer: Technical fixes register in weeks; content and citation work compounds over 60–90 days and keeps compounding.

aiSearchVisibility.headline: When someone asks ChatGPT for the best option in your market — are you the answer?

aiAutomation.problem: Quoting, intake, scheduling, data entry, reporting — every business has hours of repeatable work buried in its week. We find it, price what it's costing you, and build automation that fits the systems you already run, including the legacy ones nobody wants to touch.

demo.heading: The math on one workflow.

total.label: Cost of one workflow, per year

demo.note: Before counting the deals lost to slow turnaround.
demo.closing: An automation that cuts that by 60% pays for a typical build inside a year. We put those numbers in front of you before you commit, not after.

steps.label: Find it
steps.body: The audit locates the hours: intake, quoting, scheduling, data entry, reporting.

steps.label: Price it
steps.body: What the manual version costs you annually, sourced and sensitivity-tested.

steps.label: Build it
steps.body: Integrated with the systems you already run, including the legacy ones. Fixed price.

steps.label: Run it
steps.body: We operate and maintain it (from $1,800/mo), or hand it over fully documented. Your choice.

measurement.heading: Hours are countable.
measurement.body: Every automation ships with its own counter: runs completed, hours saved, exceptions flagged. The ROI claim from the proposal becomes a dashboard you can check any morning.

faq.question: Our systems are old. Is that a problem?
faq.answer: Usually not. Legacy integration is normal work for us, and the audit flags anything genuinely incompatible before you spend a dollar.

faq.question: What if the automation breaks?
faq.answer: Everything we build fails safe (work queues, alerts — never silent loss) and the operation retainer includes monitoring and fixes.

aiAutomation.headline: Your team does work a system should be doing.

webDevelopment.problem: Most agency websites are a brochure about quality. Ours is the evidence: run this site through Crawlmouse, check the Lighthouse scores, view the source. We build fast, accessible, search-ready sites — and we're comfortable being judged by our own.

demo.heading: Inspect this site.

steps.label: Scope
steps.body: Pages, integrations, content plan, and target metrics agreed in writing before a line is written.

steps.label: Build
steps.body: Modern stack, performance budgets enforced in CI, accessibility as a requirement, not a pass.

steps.body: Lighthouse, Crawlmouse, and rich-results checks, with the reports handed to you.

measurement.heading: Judged by the same tools we sell.

faq.question: WordPress or custom?
faq.answer: Whatever the requirements justify. We'll recommend the cheapest thing that genuinely meets them, and put the reasoning in the scope.

faq.question: Do you do redesigns or only new builds?
faq.answer: Both. Redesigns start with an audit of what's working so we don't throw away rankings you already earned.

faq.question: Who owns the site?
faq.answer: You do — code, content, accounts, everything.

webDevelopment.headline: You're reading our portfolio right now.

softwareDevelopment.problem: We design and build custom software and AI applications to production standard — specced against your workflow, integrated with your stack, and owned by you when it ships. No per-seat ransom, no black boxes.

demo.heading: Built to production standard, sized to your operation.
demo.body: The systems we build for clients are the same class of software we ship for ourselves: a live SaaS product and a health app in daily use. Same standards: typed code, tests, CI, monitoring, security review. The difference is yours is specced against your workflow, and you own it.

steps.label: Audit first
steps.body: Custom software is quoted only after the audit, because the spec IS the audit's output.

steps.label: Spec
steps.body: A written scope with acceptance criteria you can hold us to.

steps.label: Build
steps.body: Fixed price, staged delivery, working software at every stage.

steps.label: Own
steps.body: Handover with code, docs, and training, or we run it for you.

price.note: A focused operational system — a scheduler, portal, or monitoring module. Multi-system programs are phased.

measurement.heading: Acceptance criteria, in writing, before we build.
measurement.body: The scope document defines what “done” means measurably. You check the criteria yourself.

faq.question: Why won't you quote without an audit?
faq.answer: Because a number without analysis is a guess, and guesses become change orders. The audit makes the quote fixed and real, and it's credited.

faq.question: What stack do you use?
faq.answer: Chosen per project, biased toward boring, maintainable, and hireable-for. The spec states it and why.

faq.question: What does "typically $15,000–$45,000" cover?
faq.answer: A focused operational system — a scheduler, portal, or monitoring module. Multi-system programs are phased so each stage pays for itself.

crawlmouse.heading: Paste a URL. Get an honest grade.
crawlmouse.tagline: Crawlmouse grades how well your website's pages link to each other — the thing that decides whether Google and AI tools like ChatGPT can actually find your content — and shows you exactly what to fix. 250+ audits run across nearly 200 sites.

features.title: A–F internal-linking grade
features.body: Calibrated bands, not vibes. Same site, same answer, every time.

features.title: AI-readiness score
features.body: Audits the static HTML that GPTBot, Claude, and Perplexity actually read. If AI crawlers can't see your content, you'll know.

features.title: Orphan pages & click depth
features.body: Every page nothing links to, and every page buried too deep to matter.

features.title: Prioritized findings
features.body: Severity and the percentage of pages affected on every issue, so you fix what matters first.

features.title: Honest limits
features.body: When a site can't be measured properly — too small, blocked, JavaScript-only shell — Crawlmouse says so instead of inventing a grade. A tool that admits what it can't see is a tool you can trust.

audience: Built for site owners, marketers, and agencies who want the truth about their site structure without a sales call attached.

storyParagraphs: Nahl (نحل) is Arabic for honeybee — small, relentless, and useful far beyond its size.

Nahl Technologies was started by two immigrants who came to the United States with little more than a plan to learn. Udaay Sikder earned his BS and MS in Computer Science here and has spent his career in the tech industry; Mohieminul Khan earned his PhD in Mechanical Engineering and brings five years of industry experience. One of us builds software; the other builds systems. Together, that's the point.

We're proudly based in Indiana and we work with businesses everywhere, across the United States and around the world, helping them adopt AI and put it to work. We build with AI in every part of our own operation; that is how the company runs. The products we've shipped, the research we publish, and this website itself are the proof we'd rather show than tell.
The American dream, as far as we can tell, still works. You just have to build it.
